SWANDEF.book: About ₹6,500 cr firm order book at 30 Sep 2026: 6 chemical tankers (Rederiet Stenersen), 4 ammonia dual-fuel bulk carriers (Energy ONE), 4 harbour tugs (Svitzer), 1 training ship (Royal Navy of Oman). Includes government subsidy; converted at USD/INR 95.15.
SWANDEF.cover: About 30x current revenue run rate (H1 revenue ₹99 cr). Management says visibility runs to FY31; the bulk carriers deliver from FY30. Revenue has to ramp many-fold for the book to be worked off.
SWANDEF.guidance: No numeric revenue or margin guidance found. Capacity expansion of about ₹3,500 cr and a ₹4,250 cr Gujarat Maritime Board MoU were announced earlier, with up to ₹1,000 cr debentures.
SWANDEF.execution: Revenue ₹68.9 cr in Q2, up 74% year on year; EBITDA ₹11.9 cr against ₹2.9 cr. Yard restarted after insolvency resolution, so there is no long delivery record yet.
SWANDEF.driver: Export shipbuilding (tankers, tugs, green-fuel bulk carriers) and a defence export order from Oman.
SWANDEF.risks: Reported H1 profit of ₹525 cr is not operating: the company posted a pre-tax loss of ₹38 cr for the half, so the growth score here overstates quality. Delivery on first-of-kind vessels, funding of the capacity build, FX on a USD book.
SWANDEF.take: Order book is huge against today's scale, but earnings so far are not proof of execution. Treat the growth score as unreliable for this stock.

ROSSTECH.asof: Q2 FY27 (Sep 2026) revenue; order book as of Jun 2026, read 13 Nov 2026
ROSSTECH.book: Order book about ₹800 cr at 30 Jun 2026 (₹715 cr at Mar 2026). Separate long-term strategic agreements above ₹3,000 cr, which are not firm orders. Q1 also had bids above ₹350 cr and purchase orders of ₹240 cr.
ROSSTECH.cover: Roughly 1.1 years of current revenue (annualised Q2 revenue about ₹743 cr). The September order book was not found.
ROSSTECH.guidance: No numeric guidance found; management describes the pipeline and capacity expansion as supporting continued growth.
ROSSTECH.execution: Revenue ₹185.7 cr in Q2, up 48%; Q1 was ₹154.7 cr, up 78%, with PBT up 139%. Four straight quarters of rising revenue.
ROSSTECH.driver: Aerospace and defence electronics and wiring for global OEMs; new semiconductor customer; space programmes; US subsidiary milestones.
ROSSTECH.risks: Customer concentration (Boeing was flagged at about 40% of revenue), thin cover if inflows slow, margin stability as costs rise.
ROSSTECH.take: Growth is real and the book is being replenished, but cover is about a year. Watch the next order-book figure.

PTCIL.asof: Q1 FY27 (Jun 2026), read 13 Nov 2026; Q2 not found
PTCIL.book: Order book size not disclosed in what I found. Recent wins: Airbus titanium castings agreement (A320neo, A330neo, A350; 6 Aug 2026), BrahMos Aerospace missile sub-system, ARDE/DRDO titanium cradle for the light tank, Gun Factory Kanpur gun components, VSSC titanium ingots.
PTCIL.cover: Cannot be computed without a disclosed book.
PTCIL.guidance: An aggregator reports management targeting revenue doubling in FY27; not confirmed from a primary source. ₹1,800 cr QIP approved to fund capex and acquisitions.
PTCIL.execution: Consolidated income ₹197 cr in Q1, up 83%; PAT ₹29 cr against ₹5 cr; EBITDA margin about 27.5% against 18%. The titanium subsidiary Aerolloy runs about 45% EBITDA margin.
PTCIL.driver: Titanium and superalloy castings for aerospace and defence, import substitution, move from components to sub-systems.
PTCIL.risks: Very rich valuation, finance costs up 117% on higher borrowing, serial-qualification risk with global primes, dilution from the QIP.
PTCIL.take: Margin expansion is the strongest in this batch. Order book and guidance still need a primary-source check, and the Q2 result should be read when out.

KROSS.book: No order book figure disclosed. Management refers to a healthy order book and rising trailer and tractor volumes. At Q3 FY26 the axle order book was about 4,000 axles a month.
KROSS.cover: Not computable; this is a volume business with short order cycles.
KROSS.guidance: No formal revenue guidance. Earlier commentary pointed to margins moving toward about 15% as new capacity and exports scale; a new project completes around Q4 FY27 with revenue from FY28.
KROSS.execution: Revenue ₹235 cr in Q2, up 80%; PAT ₹19.7 cr, up 144%; operating margin 13%. H1 revenue ₹419 cr. FY26 revenue was up only 8.5%, so this is a sharp cyclical upturn.
KROSS.driver: Trailer and tractor axle demand recovery, capacity additions, new products and exports.
KROSS.risks: Cyclical commercial-vehicle demand, small company, growth rate flattered by a weak base last year.
KROSS.take: Good operating leverage on a demand rebound. There is no order book to underwrite it, so it depends on the cycle holding.

KABRAEXTRU.book: No order book figure disclosed in the Q2 presentation. Earlier items: about ₹133 cr energy-storage order (Feb 2026) and a clean-energy order book of about ₹150 cr cited at Q1.
KABRAEXTRU.guidance: No guidance found; no concall transcript for Q2.
KABRAEXTRU.execution: Revenue ₹221 cr in Q2, up 64%, with the Geon division up 2.5x to ₹166 cr. PAT only ₹4 cr (about 2% of revenue) against ₹0.3 cr. Q1 FY27 was still a loss, with battery-division losses. A Daman plant stoppage in July from flooding.
KABRAEXTRU.driver: Energy storage and battery packs, plus the Geon division, on top of plastic extrusion machinery.
KABRAEXTRU.risks: Thin margin, battery division still losing money, project-based revenue recognised on commissioning, very high P/E on tiny profit.
KABRAEXTRU.take: The growth score of 88 comes from a near-zero profit base. Order visibility is the weakest here; this is a turnaround, not an order-book compounder.
